hero.lede: PowerBGInfo is an Evotec PowerShell module that puts machine details, charts and small topology diagrams on Windows desktop and lock-screen wallpapers. ChartForgeX draws the whole image, from the generated backdrop to the last chart label.
hero.alt: Server status wallpaper rendered by PowerBGInfo: the host name SQL-PROD-01 with its role and owner, four tiles for uptime, CPU, memory and network, and panels for volumes, network throughput and critical services.

scenarios.title: Four wallpapers, each with one job
scenarios.body: Each script answers one question for the person in front of the screen and renders in light and dark at any resolution. They share one look, defined once in HudTheme.ps1: the same margins, glass panels, type scale and status colours. The values are fixed samples so anyone can reproduce the renders; comments in the scripts show where real values come from, such as Get-Counter or Get-Volume. Under each wallpaper is the New-BGInfo call that places what it shows; the full script is one click away.

alts.server-status: Server status wallpaper for SQL-PROD-01: role, owner, maintenance window and on-call address, tiles for uptime, CPU, memory and network, and panels for volume usage, network throughput and running services.
alts.helpdesk: Help desk wallpaper: how to reach the service desk, its portal, hours and current service status, with tiles for asset tag, computer name, IP address, signed-in user and Windows version.
alts.classroom: Lab wallpaper for seat LAB-B-14: a large seat name, the nightly reset time, the instructor and Wi-Fi details, and panels for session time left, completed exercises and class progress.
alts.admin-workstation: Privileged access workstation wallpaper for PAW-T0-03: seven health tiles, a privileged sign-in chart, a topology of the allowed path from the workstation through a jump host to tier 0, a tier 0 change trend and open security alerts.

parts.title: What ChartForgeX draws
parts.body: PowerBGInfo collects the values, lays out the wallpaper and applies it through Windows. Every pixel of the image comes from ChartForgeX; there is no System.Drawing or browser underneath.

items.title: Charts
items.body: Thirteen chart kinds, from sparklines and gauges to progress bars and pictorial rows, on panels with the corner radius and border of the rest of the wallpaper.

items.title: Topology
items.body: Groups, nodes and links with status and replication lag, drawn by the same TopologyChart that renders service maps in .NET.

items.title: Canvas and backdrop
items.body: Info tiles with icons, mini charts and progress, and generated backdrops of gradients, glows and grid or dot patterns, composed with VisualCanvas and ImageComposition.

items.title: One theme
items.body: Charts, topology and tiles each take a light or dark mode and draw text with the ChartForgeX text engine, so a wallpaper reads as one design instead of three overlays.

start.title: Get started
start.body: Install the module from the PowerShell Gallery and render to a file first, so you can check the layout before anything changes on a desktop.
